title: Run-based day recovery used fewer queries for masked ozone episode labels in four US bird-survey samples from 2005 to 2019
abstract: We tested a rule that recovers hidden days in the largest number of possible three-day ozone runs. We used 797 complete two-site windows before US bird surveys in four region-period samples from 2005 to 2019. Each trial hid six dates per site. Across 50 trials per window, the rule used 19.8-20.4% fewer queries than random recovery of relevant days for consecutive gaps and 6.5-8.3% fewer for scattered gaps. A complete all-low reference explains part of the gain without pollution episodes. All recovered labels matched hidden truth. This is a data recovery method test, not an ecological effect estimate. Artificial gaps, selected complete records, equal recovery costs and assumed correct daily labels limit wider use. The package includes code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure and a verified external-input recipe.

display.caption: Queries to certify ozone episode labels under artificial gaps in four selected US bird-survey samples.

citations.reason: We reuse verified daily evidence and survey windows. The source records overlap. We test a recovery policy, not natural missing-day bounds.
